name: WebMainBench (545-page subset with calibrated Markdown ground truth)
attribution: OpenDataLab, WebMainBench, introduced in 'Dripper: Token-Efficient Main HTML Extraction with a Lightweight LM', arXiv:2511.23119
layout: corpora/webmainbench/test/{html/NNNN.html.gz,ground-truth/NNNN.json}: NNNN is the 1-based line number; ground_truth.main_markdown is groundtruth_content verbatim, main_content the same text with link and image targets removed; the page type is meta.level (simple, mid, hard). The full 7,809-page file is not used: its ground truth is tag-level, not Markdown.
annotationMarkers: The source html fields were saved from the annotation tool and carry the answer key: on 544 of 545 pages, every element selected as main content has cc-select="true" and the class token mark-selected (103,675 elements), and every page has an injected <style id="cc-extraStyle"> that highlights them (in <head> on 544 pages, in <body> on page 0313). Since October 10, 2026 (after the extraction-rerun runs), the prepare tool strips all three and refuses a page that still has any. Two other traces of the tool are kept, since they carry no selection: data-anno-uid, on selected and unselected elements alike (about 341,000 unselected), and the class cc-unloaded, on 1,776 image, video and audio elements across 112 pages (278 of them selected). The runs extraction-rerun-wmb-2026-10-10T15-14-27-287Z-8ec849 and markdown-wmb-2026-10-10T15-15-30-344Z-d7971d read the unstripped HTML; no candidate or lab code reads these markers, and rs-trafilatura, dom-smoothie and lol-html give identical output on the stripped and unstripped HTML (the Node Readability adapter was not compared).
